findings.location: architecture/w02-notes-errata/README.md PERF-032-F F15 bullet ('identities are taken with the `id` bound at import' ... 'Not excluded: a change the identity snapshot cannot see (...) that leaves every corpus answer unchanged, and any change triggered by anything other than the exec and the corpus calls'); Round-4 dispositions row C4-1; scripts/perf032_followup.py module docstring F15 item, _ID, check_unique_oracle
findings.finding: The restated F15 residual is still not exact. The executed bytes run inside check_unique_oracle's own frame, so they can rebind the check itself through sys._getframe(1). Three exec-triggered probes return 773 and are outside both stated exclusions (/private/tmp/claude-501/cleanup-review-r5/probes/f15r5.py <name>, one fresh process each). (1) checker_require sets f_globals['require'] = lambda c, m: None, then rebinds _utils.uniq and _keywords.uniq to lambda c: True and defines unique = lambda c: True. It is ACCEPTED 773. Afterwards stock uniq([1, 1]) is True, and Draft 2020-12, 7 and 4 all accept [1, 1], which is a corpus input. So this change alters every duplicate corpus answer, made by the exec. It falls under neither 'leaves every corpus answer unchanged' nor 'triggered by anything other than the exec'. It is also the '_keywords.uniq ... rebinding' that the bullet lists as refused. (2) corpus_locals rewrites f_locals' corpus, expected and valid lists in place to 773 empty arrays answered True and sets unique = lambda c: True. It is ACCEPTED 773, so 'every answer of the reviewed unique ... must equal the stock answer' over the 773-array corpus is not what was checked. (3) checker_id rebinds f_globals['_ID'] to hide the round-4 rebuilt uniq, which is wrong for duplicate ints >= 5. It is ACCEPTED 773, and stock Draft 2020-12 then accepts [5, 5]. So 'identities are taken with the id bound at import' holds only while the bytes leave the module global alone; the comment beside _ID likewise names only builtins.id. Probe (3) arguably falls under the first exclusion, but probes (1) and (2) do not. A smaller ambiguity: draft4_type_checker mutates Draft4Validator.TYPE_CHECKER in place (a different object from the Draft 2020-12 one). It is ACCEPTED 773, and Draft 4 uniqueItems then accepts [1, 1]. That case is inside the limit only if 'every corpus answer' means the three checked answer sets (reviewed unique, stock uniq, the Draft 2020-12 verdict), which the text does not say. Every positive coverage claim, and every named refusal, holds when the bytes do not touch the check. The merged byte pin of the reviewed bytes refuses all of these, so the pipeline is unaffected. The finding is about the stated limit only, which the owner rule requires to be exact.
findings.requiredChange: Make the residual open-ended and name the check itself, in the README F15 bullet, the module docstring and the C4-1 row. For example: 'The check refuses the named changes, made by bytes that do not also alter the check. Nothing else is excluded. In particular, the bytes run in the check's own frame and can rebind its globals (require, _ID), its locals (corpus, expected, valid) or the builtins it calls, after which any change passes, including one that changes corpus answers. Also not excluded: a change the snapshot cannot see that leaves the checked answers (reviewed unique, stock uniq, a Draft 2020-12 validator) unchanged, such as another draft's TYPE_CHECKER state, and any change triggered other than by the exec and the corpus calls.' Qualify 'identities are taken with the id bound at import' the same way, or drop it. No code change is required. Running the exec in a separate process is optional tightening and does not remove the need to state the limit.
